properties.bedrock_geology: Lower Carboniferous (Tournaisian/Visean) Calders Member of the Strathclyde Group (sandstone, siltstone, and mudstone) intruded by quartz-dolerite sills
properties.superficial_deposits: Glacial till (boulder clay) and Devensian glaciolacustrine sands overlying steep river valley incisions
properties.topography: North-facing steep declivity dropping sharply into the deeply incised Water of Leith gorge, stabilizing the northern boundary of the New Town plateau
properties.soil_class: Brown earths with well-drained loam across terraced domestic plots; moisture-retentive alluvium along river bluffs

properties.architectural_style: Georgian / Greek Revival (James Gillespie Graham, master plan c. 1822)

structures.name: Moray Place Northern Crescent Terraces (Nos. 31-36)
structures.roof_material: Scotch and Welsh blue-grey slate mansards with lead valleys and heavy sandstone chimney stacks
structures.fenestration: 12-pane timber sash and case windows with cast-iron balconettes, rusticated lower ashlar courses, and canted stone bay extrusions to the rear

structures.name: Terraced Rear Mews & Sub-Level Vaulted Outbuildings

properties.infrastructural_elements: Curved sandstone parapets, steep retaining terrace walls descending to rear private garden plots, boundary stone copings, and cast-iron spearhead railings

properties.vegetation_strata: Dense mature deciduous canopy on steep valley embankment leading down to Dean Gardens and the Water of Leith
properties.understory: Hedera helix (Common Ivy), bramble thickets, and manicured terrace lawn grass with ornamental rhododendrons

properties.lighting_regime: Diffused late afternoon cool northern skylight balanced by soft low-angle western solar grazing, illuminating soot-patinated sandstone ashlar textures
properties.sensory_profile: Distant rushing waters of the Water of Leith echoing through the gorge, damp earth scent from mature beech leaf litter, cold crisp Scottish maritime breeze, chimney downdraft soot notes
